newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says "positively" seeking New York listing.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says "positively" seeking New York listing.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Tuesday that it is "positively" seeking to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange, but added that it has not set any target year for the move.

"We're positively looking into the possibility, but we have not yet decided anything concrete. We have not set any target year for the move," a company spokesman told Reuters when asked about a Japanese newspaper report on Tuesday that Toyota is seeking the New York listing by 2000.
By listing its shares in New York, Toyota wants to gain a reputation as a "global corporation" rather than seeking to raise funds, the company spokesman said.
Toyota plans to set up an internal team to prepare for the listing, the spokesman said.
The mass-circulation daily Yomiuri Shimbun quoted Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda as saying in an interview that the company hopes to list its shares in New York by 2000 to improve its global image.

"The issue of disclosure would be difficult," Okuda was quoted as saying. But he added: "We have already reached an internal consensus that doing so is necessary for the purpose of our public relations. We hope to be listed by 2000."

Toyota would come under strict scrutiny from the Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) and would need to win the body's approval for the listing. Toyota aims to set up a special team within the company soon to prepare the financial data needed for the listing, the newspaper said.

Toyota has set 2000 as the target year for the listing because it believes it will be able to show itself to be a global company to overseas investors by that time, the newspaper said. It is due to complete its current plan for expanding overseas production in 1997 and is looking to expand output in China and India by 2000, it said.
At present 11 Japanese companies are listed on the New York exchange and Honda Motor Co Ltd is the sole car manufacturer among them, the newspaper said.
As of 0124 GMT, Toyota's shares were up 30 yen at 3,190 yen on turnover of 1.24 million shares.
Blue-chip stocks such as Toyota have remained relatively strong despite the overall gloom in the Tokyo market.
The key Nikkei average was down 71.98 points or 0.41 percent at 17,409.16 in late morning trade on Tuesday.
